statement: Let T be any finite simple tree of order n>=2 and diameter at most three, and let Phi_T(z)=sum_{k=1}^n s_k(T) z^k, where s_k(T) counts nonempty connected induced vertex subsets of cardinality k, each counted once. Every complex zero z of Phi_T satisfies 1/2<=|z+1/2|<=1/2+(n-1)^(1/(n-1)). The zero z=0 is simple and is the only zero on the inner boundary. A zero lies on the outer boundary if and only if n is even and T is the star K_{1,n-1}; in that case the unique outer-boundary zero is z=-1-(n-1)^(1/(n-1)). In particular, for every pair of integers a,b>=1, the double star D(a,b), obtained from an edge uv by attaching a leaves to u and b leaves to v, has all its nonzero subtree roots strictly between the two circles, with n=a+b+2. The frozen original claim for arbitrary trees, without a diameter restriction, remains unresolved.
contribution: A complete analytic proof of both shifted root bounds for the unrestricted two-parameter double-star family, using a convex endpoint estimate on the translated outer circle with an explicit positive domination margin. The diameter-at-most-three formulation follows by combining this family theorem with the known elementary star formula; those star facts and the known universal radial equality classification are not claimed as new. Exact finite Schur checks support but do not prove the infinite assertion. No equivalent all-double-star result was found in the bounded current primary-source screen; novelty and mathematical value remain for the fresh referee to assess.
